sites.name: 150 North Riverside
sites.note: 150 N Riverside will open the main lobby to view the 150-foot-long Media Stream. This is a self-guided experience.

sites.name: 333 South Wabash
sites.note: The lobby coffee shop, as well as the second floor food hall will be open for visitors to enjoy and access to floor 16 will afford a peek at a vacant office level with great views.

sites.name: 345 Art Gallery
sites.note: Explore the gallery's exhibit spaces and works on a self-guided tour.

sites.name: 345 N. Morgan
sites.note: 345 N. Morgan will offer access to the amenity spaces located on the 11th Floor of the building including the conservatory, conference room, and roof deck.

sites.name: 5040-5060 North Marine Drive Condominiums
sites.note: Visitors can tour the lobby, the courtyard, and one apartment unit.  Owners will be on hand to speak about the building's history and architecture, and poster boards and a video will impart more information. Visitors may take part in any or all of the activities.

sites.name: 540 W. Madison
sites.note: Visit the lobby and tenant lounge, the newly renovated 2nd floor cafe, and 6th floor roof garden. A brochure with building information will also be available.

sites.name: 6018North
sites.note: On view is the set of a recent performance "Persephone: Extraction & Metamorphosis," where artists and performers collaboratively developed a time-based, immersive experience that unfolded throughout the rooms and spaces. See the original details of the house and how it has been transformed for the show and other projects.

sites.name: Airstream Building
sites.note: Visit the trailer atop 1807 W. Sunnyside Ave.

sites.name: Al-Sadiq Mosque
sites.note:
Visitors can explore the mosque and view information on its history as well as the history of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community.

Members will be on hand to give a brief introduction of the site and also answer any questions.

sites.name: Albany-Carroll Arts Building
sites.note: Visitors will have the opportunity to explore dozens of working artist studios, meet the artists behind the work, and experience the creative process firsthand.

sites.name: All Saints' Episcopal Church
sites.note: At the top of each hour, visitors will have an opportunity to ring the restored bell historically used by the Ravenswood volunteer fire brigade.

sites.name: All Star Press
sites.note:
Visitors will have a chance to take a tour of the space and staff will assist in answering any questions. 

Visitors will take a self-guided tour with art experts in the vicinity to explain the process of screen-printing, as well as guide visitors through the studio space. Demonstrations may take place.

sites.name: Alliance Française de Chicago
sites.note: Both levels of the Chicago Avenue building will be open, and the library on the Dearborn side as well.

sites.name: Annunciation Greek Orthodox Cathedral of Chicago
sites.note: A station-by-station brochure will be available with a guide to answer questions at each station.

sites.name: Anti-Cruelty
sites.note: The lobby and adoption floors are open for visitors to enjoy a self-guided tour of the signature architectural elements. Visitors are welcome to spend time with the animals while onsite, or participate in the Reading Buddies program, where guests help pets relax by reading a provided book to them. Adoptions are also available!

sites.name: AS+GG Architecture
sites.address: 30 W. Monroe St., Suite 400, Chicago, IL 60603
sites.note: Visit the studio on the fourth floor of the Inland Steel Building at 30 West Monroe. The open office environment encourages exploration, allowing guests to enjoy a self-guided tour of the space. Architects and designers will be stationed throughout the studio, including near project models, in the library, at video displays, and in conference areas, to answer questions and share insights about the firm's work. In the building lobby, visitors can view Radiant I, the renowned sculpture by Richard Lippold.

sites.name: Aspire Center for Workforce Innovation
sites.note: Public spaces including the plaza, roof terrace, lobby, mezzanine, and corridors will be open to visitors. A special exhibit highlights the transformation of Emmet School, the cultural impact of the West Side, and larger changes within the Austin neighborhood. Also on view: a 120-foot mural depicting the history of the West Side, highlighting innovations in healthcare, dedication to civic engagement, and Black leadership.

sites.name: Assumption Greek Orthodox Church
sites.note: Mandatory 10-minute tours of the main church and chapel will be offered by Church members. No admittance to choir loft.

sites.name: Avalon Regal Theater
sites.note: The grand lobby and auditorium will be open for viewing.

sites.name: Avondale Bowl
sites.note:
Volunteers will escort guests from the front door to either the stairway or elevators leading to the bowling alley. Guests are encouraged to take a self-guided tour of the lanes and bar while stopping by the Shoe Counter to have any questions answered about the space.

The bowling alley will be accessible for photos as well as the bar. Guests will be asked to borrow a pair of bowling shoes if they plan on going up on the wood approaches to take pictures. Staff will be at the shoe counter to share historical details and answer any questions.

sites.name: BandWith Chicago
sites.note: The entire building will be open including the coffee shop, music library, rehearsal spaces, and recording studio. Optional guided tours will be provided, but visitors can also enjoy a self-guided experience.

sites.name: Beverly Hills Tennis Club
sites.note: Guests may explore the clubhouse meeting room, kitchen, locker rooms, outdoor patio and deck. Visitors will not be able to play tennis, but will be shown the courts.

sites.name: Birch Road Clubhouse
sites.note: Groups of 10-12 people will be given tours of the entire clubhouse.

sites.name: bKL Architecture
sites.address: 225 N. Columbus Dr., Suite 100, Chicago, IL 60601
sites.note: The studio will be open for self-guided tours. Staff will be available to answer any questions.

sites.name: Blackhawks Ice Center
sites.note: The Ice Center will be open for self-guided tours.

sites.name: Boxville
sites.note: All or most shipping container-based enterprises will be open and accessible to visitors. There will also be a range of activities, including music, open air cooking, and more.

sites.name: Broadway In Chicago's Cadillac Palace Theatre
sites.note: Visitors may explore the main lobby and the orchestra level seating area (no stage access). From the orchestra level seating area, you can view the entire theater space.

sites.name: Bronzeville Black Metropolis National Heritage Area
sites.note: Visitors will have the opportunity to view a video about the National Heritage Areas and Bronzeville landmarks as described by Bronzeville docents, tour guides, and historians. The video will play hourly starting at 11:00 am.

sites.name: Bubbly + Norwich
sites.note: Visitors will have a self-guided experience, and participating businesses and organizations will have their studios and workshops open.

sites.name: Buddhist Temple of Chicago
sites.note: The entire temple will be open. Guests will be greeted in the lobby/reception area and taken on a tour. Blueprints of the space will be on view, accompanied by historical and architectural information from temple members. Guests are invited to take part in guided tours, and may also look around on their own.

sites.name: BUILD Headquarters
sites.note: Visitors may take a self-guided tour of the building's three levels and urban farm.

sites.name: Canopy
sites.address: 180 W Washington Street, Suite 200, Chicago, IL 60602
sites.note: Visitors will have the chance to explore the building's history and engage with the architectural practice's current and upcoming work through project drawings, photos, models, renderings, and current material selections. Architects will be on site.

sites.name: Carl Schurz High School
sites.note: Visitors are invited to explore on their own. Guided tours may be offered in addition.

sites.name: Casa Bonita
sites.note: Guided tours are mandatory and include: the sunken courtyard, hallways with terrazzo floors, party room, indoor swimming pool, exercise room, children's playroom, and refinishing room.

sites.name: Center for Native Futures
sites.address: 56 W. Adams St., Suite 102, Chicago, IL 60603
sites.note: Visit the exhibition, “Pocket Full of Shells,” an artistic family showcase, and take part in select activities. Artist-in-residence Jason Wesaw may be onsite as well to offer studio tours and engage with visitors.

sites.name: Charles H. Shaw Technology and Learning Center
sites.note:
There will be four tours each day, beginning at 11 a.m., with the last tour at 2 p.m. Each tour will include all campus spaces, including the Sears Sunken Garden, the Powerhouse, and Nichols Tower.
If a visitor misses a scheduled tour, they may pick up a map at the Sunken Garden (weather permitting) or at the Tower and complete a self-guided tour of the three sites.

sites.name: Chicago Architecture Center
sites.note: Enjoy free Center admission, including all exhibit spaces. Come shop the Design Store as well.

sites.name: Chicago Architecture Center Marquette Hub
sites.note:
The Marquette Hub will be open with opportunities to see the CAC's new satellite location, buy tickets to future CAC walking and building tours, shop at the Design Store, and have any OHC questions answered by staff.

Visitors may also explore the lobby-adjacent exhibition “Nwi Yathmomen, We will tell our story,” curated by visual artist Andrea Carlson (Ojibwe) and historian John Low (Pokagon Band of Potawatomi). The exhibition addresses the representation of Native people in the architectural design elements of the building and asserts the presence of Native peoples, and particularly Potawatomi people, in Chicago.

sites.name: Chicago Industrial Arts & Design Center
sites.note: CIADC has four workshops spanning four floors that visitors will be able to explore at their own pace, seeing the building and work activity. Please respect people working in the space by keeping a safe distance.

sites.name: Chicago Loop Synagogue
sites.note: The main sanctuary will be open to visitors along with the lower level beit medresh.

sites.name: Chicago Magic Lounge
sites.note:
Visitors will tour the Chicago Magic Lounge in small groups, with a guide who will explain the artifacts, ephemera, posters, and architecture. There may be a short wait for your tour to begin.

Please note: this is an architectural and historical tour, there will be no magic performances.

sites.name: Chicago Maritime Museum
sites.note: The museum galleries and store will be open for self-guided exploration, with volunteer docents available to assist visitors.

sites.name: Chicago Printmakers Collaborative
sites.note: Throughout the day, demonstrations of etching, screen printing, lithography, and relief will be given by Hiroshi Ariyama, Deborah Maris Lader, Mary O'Connor, and Lauren Steinert. The studio will also have a craft station for all ages to create something they can take home with them. The gallery currently hosts the "Stone Age" Lithography Showcase along with art from all over the world.

sites.name: Chinese American Museum of Chicago
sites.note: The museum is open on the first, second, and fourth floors, and is a self guided experience. The first floor gallery will host the show "Garden Farms," and second floor holds the permanent exhibition "Great Wall to Great Lakes: Chinese Immigration to the Midwest." The fourth floor consists of a reading room, and the Spotlight Series gallery, which features work by emerging and mid-career artists, and an exhibition called "Light Light Light" with work by the artist Percy Lam.

sites.name: Chinese American Service League Kam Liu Building
sites.note:
Visitors can choose between station-by-station exploration or guided tours. Tours will offer access to more areas of the building.

Guided Tours
10:30am | 12:00pm | 1:30pm | 3:00pm (Saturday only)
Walk through CASL’s building and hear how its architecture reflects its mission to serve Chicago’s Chinese American and broader AAPI community.

Gallery Exhibit
On view all weekend: a gallery showcasing CASL’s history and its impact on Chinatown through architecture.

sites.name: Christ the Savior Orthodox Church
sites.note: The main floor of the church will be open. Optional guided tours will be provided by church volunteers. The entrance to the altar space is restricted.

sites.name: Church of the Atonement Episcopal
sites.note: The church will be open, with self-guided tours. Guests may also visit the Elizabethan Room in the parish house.

sites.name: Church of the Holy Family
sites.note: Visitors are welcome to tour the church and enjoy a self-guided tour of the first floor. Photography is allowed and staff will be on hand to answer questions.

sites.name: Climate Action Museum
sites.note:
The museum will be open for guided or self-guided tours. Guided tours will be a station-by-station experience.

Enjoy free popcorn, grab a CAM button or sticker while supplies last, and enter a drawing for a single-burner induction cooktop.

sites.name: Columbia Yacht Club
sites.address: 111 N. Lake Shore Dr., Chicago, IL 60601
sites.note: Visitors are invited to take self-guided tours of member areas. There will be printed materials, and volunteer members will be stationed throughout to offer insights.

sites.name: Colvin House
sites.note: Guided tours will be provided.

sites.name: DANK Haus German American Cultural Center
sites.note: All six floors and the roof terrace of the DANK Haus will be open, with some restrictions. A guided tour is available if visitors would like to participate, however they may do a self-guided tour.

sites.name: David Rubenstein Forum at the University of Chicago
sites.note: Visitors will enjoy self-guided tours of the building.

sites.name: DePaul University Holtschneider Performance Center - Jarvis Opera Hall
sites.note: This year features the Sasha Gerritson and Eugene Jarvis Opera Hall. With an audience capacity of 160, the Jarvis Opera Hall provides a beautifully intimate opera experience. Staff will be onsite to answer questions about the space.

sites.name: Ebenezer Missionary Baptist Church
sites.note: Visitors may enjoy a guided or self guided tour of the main sanctuary and all accessory rooms. This involves stairs to the balcony in the sanctuary or to the second floor in the attached building.

sites.name: Edgewater History Museum
sites.note: The Edgewater History Museum provides a compact, self-guided visitor experience. Docents are available to answer questions and provide guidance.

sites.name: Electrical Audio
sites.note: Visitors will line up outside for short guided tours for 20-30 people. There is no self-guided option.

sites.name: Eris Brewery & Cider House
sites.address: 4240 W. Irving Park Rd., Chicago, IL 60641
sites.note:
Please note: most staff will be focused on service to restaurant guests rather than OHC. Questions about the building should be directed to volunteers wearing OHC t-shirts.

Visitors will be provided a booklet with building information and map for a 15-20 minute self-guided tour. Optional guided tours will include areas of the building not open to the public. These areas are not wheelchair accessible.

sites.name: Farm on Ogden
sites.note: Visitors will be provided with a map to lead them through self-guided tour stations. There will also be interpretive signage and staff near the designated stations to share more information.

sites.name: FarmZero
sites.address: 30 N. LaSalle St., Suite 1800, Chicago, IL 60602
sites.note:
Guided tours of six guests at a time are mandatory in the grow room given food safety responsibilities. Live harvesting and packing of edible flowers and microgreens will be on view, and samples of microgreens will be offered.

There will also be a station-by-station experience in the office space and processing room.

sites.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago and Money Museum
sites.note:
Visitors will enjoy exclusive access to the Great Hall, a space not normally open to the public. Explore on your own or enjoy brief presentations from Chicago Fed volunteers. At the Money Museum, visitors can try their hand at detecting counterfeit notes, learn what a million dollars looks like, and view the rare currency on display. There will also be a temporary exhibit on display: A Century of Route 66 - Driving Culture and Commerce. 

Visitor entry will conclude at 4:30 PM each day.

sites.name: Field Notes Brand
sites.note:
The retail shop, main design studio, and warehouse space will be open for viewing. 

Visitors will be able to visit the gift shop and see the main design studio/ work space and warehouse/ pack and ship area.

sites.name: Fine Arts Building
sites.note: Visitors will enjoy a self-guided tour through all 10 floors of the Fine Arts Building, exploring the majestic architecture, history, and creativity of this 19th-century Chicago landmark.

sites.name: First Church of Deliverance
sites.note: Visitors may explore the first floor sanctuary, foyer, and exterior areas, with recorded audio guide provided. Additionally, FCD music products such as CDs, Vinyl, and music books are available by suggested donation.

sites.name: First Presbyterian Church of Chicago
sites.note:
Visitors are invited to explore the architecture, history, and ongoing transformation of a landmark that has served Chicago for nearly two centuries while embracing new possibilities for art, neighborhood life, and public engagement.

The campus will also feature a dynamic program of contemporary arts and cultural activities. Visitors may encounter site-specific visual art installations, artist activations, live performances, open studios, chef-led culinary programming, and other community-centered experiences as part of First Church's ongoing partnership with the Chicago Architecture Center through the Built on Belief initiative.

sites.name: First United Methodist Church at the Chicago Temple
sites.address: 77 W. Washington St., Lobby Level, Chicago, IL 60602
sites.note: Visitors are invited to take self-guided tours of the lobby and Sanctuary. The Sky Chapel is available to tour on other occasions as listed on the church's website.

sites.name: Florence Lowden Miller Historic Pullman Center
sites.note:
Visitors can explore the building’s first floor and collections on display.Guided tours will depart at 11 AM, 12 PM, 1 PM, 2 PM, and 3 PM. Tours end near the Historic Pullman Foundation Exhibit Hall, also open during OHC weekend.


11 AM, 1 PM, and 3 PM: The Four Stories Tour
A short walk through the town the Pullman Company built, touching on urban planning, rail innovation, labor history, and civil rights, and why this place matters to Chicago and U.S. history.


12 PM and 2 PM: Labor History Tour
The story of the 1894 Pullman strike, how it grew into a national railroad boycott, and its legacy.

sites.name: Four Star Mushrooms
sites.note:
Visitors can walk the grow-room corridor and see a controlled environment agriculture operation up close, with staff on hand to answer questions. Fresh mushroom punnets, mushroom coffee, and pastries from local bakers are available for purchase, along with Four Star shirts and hats — and Mushroom Club memberships. 

Please wear closed-toe shoes.

sites.name: Fourth Presbyterian Church
sites.note: Visitors are welcome to view the Sanctuary at Michigan and Delaware and Buchanan Chapel on the second floor of the Gratz Center which is accessible from the sanctuary.

sites.name: Fraternité Notre Dame
sites.note: Guided tours and photo displays will be available.

sites.name: Gary Comer Youth Center
sites.note: Visitors will receive a guided tour of the Youth Center, including the cafe, gym/auditorium, Best Buy Teen Tech Center, Dance Studio, Exhibition Hall and Rooftop Garden. Guests will also have the opportunity to visit the GCYC farm, just across the street.

sites.name: Glessner House
sites.note: 10-minute guided tours of the main spaces on the first floor will be offered.

sites.name: Goettsch Partners
sites.address: 224 S. Michigan Ave., Floor 17, Chicago, IL 60604
sites.note: Goettsch Partners staff will take all guests through a 15-20 minute guided tour of the office, viewing recent work. Volunteers will greet guests while awaiting staff tour guides to cycle back to the lobby. There may be a brief wait when you arrive.

sites.name: Graceland Cemetery and Arboretum
sites.note:
Enjoy a lineup of activities all day at Beyond the Gates: Glimpses of Graceland! Visitors will be welcomed into Graceland beginning at 10 am when the vendor marker opens located in the main entrance parking lot and pedestrian plaza near the visitor center.

The main entrance will remain open for pedestrian or bicycle traffic only; vehicles will be required to enter at the Greenwood Gate entrance. Parking instructions will be provided at the Greenwood Gate.

At various points each day, guests can engage with various vendors, guest speakers, and docents as well as view the cemetery at their own pace or during one of the scheduled events. Please expect to pay for any art, food, or swag that you wish to purchase from the vendors onsite. All other events provided by Graceland are free to the public.

Please see link for detailed listing each day: https://tr.ee/DEW5kUfpgf

sites.name: Greater Tabernacle Cathedral
sites.address: 11300 S. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr., Chicago, IL 60628
sites.note: Visitors will be offered optional guided tours of the sanctuary, administration building, and Fellowship Hall. A self-guided, station-by-station experience is also available.

sites.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
sites.address: 5700 S. Lake Shore Dr., Chicago, IL 60637
sites.note:
OHC Visitors will be able to grab a scavenger hunt when they arrive to learn more about the architecture of the museum.

Museum admission is free on Sunday, October 18 only. Tickets are required and advanced reservations are strongly encouraged. Reserve your free tickets, use promo code OPENHOUSE. The museum will also be open on Saturday, October 17 with paid admission. Use promo code OHC20 to get 20% off General Admission tickets for Saturday.

Please note this site does not allow priority access.

sites.name: Growing Home's Wood Street Urban Farm
sites.note: All growing spaces, the processing area, and training trailers will be open.

sites.name: Guild Row
sites.note: The main campus building will be open for a guided architecture and real estate development tour with information about Guild Row's ever-evolving offerings. Food and beverage by Little Lark - a family-friendly pizza and cocktail restaurant within Guild Row - will be available for purchase before and after tours on Saturday. Little Lark will be closed on Sunday for an event - coffee, snacks & brunch drinks will be available for purchase in Guild Hall before & after tours. Guided tours are mandatory.

sites.name: Harold Washington Library Center
sites.note:
Visitors are invited to take a self-guided tour of the building's art and architecture. Beginning at the Ida B. Wells Corridor, guided tours of up to 25 people will also be offered Saturday at 11am and Sunday at 1pm highlighting the art throughout the building.

Between the hours of 10am - 4pm on Saturday and 1pm - 3:30pm on Sunday, visitors will also enjoy behind-the-scenes access to the architecturally significant Special Collections Reading Room on the 9th floor.

sites.name: Heritage Museum of Asian Art
sites.note:
Visit two newly opened exhibitions during Open House Chicago: Cutting East to West, presented with the Guild of American Papercutters and featuring papercut artworks by artists from across the United States and around the world; and Becoming Words, presented with the Seldon Institute and featuring calligraphy by Chicago-based Japanese American master Hekiun Oda and Paris-based Iranian master Dr. Bahman Panahi.


Visitors may also enjoy self-guided exploration of the museum’s permanent collection and special exhibitions, meet participating artists, view live demonstrations, and take part in hands-on art activities.


Visitors can watch live paper cutting demonstrations from 11:00 am - 3:00 pm on Saturday and Sunday.

sites.name: HKS
sites.address: 72 W. Adams St., 11th Floor, Chicago, IL 60430
sites.note: Visitors will enjoy a self-guided tour of the office. HKS designers will be on hand to answer questions. Come sketch with us!

sites.name: Holy Name Cathedral
sites.note:
Guided tours will be provided on the hour both days, and guests are welcome to join in late. Those in a guided tour will be guided throughout the Cathedral. Those on a self guided tour are asked to stay at the ground level and not walk up the stairs into the altar area. 

Visitors may take a brochure as they walk around, and optional Cathedral docent tours will be led every 30 minutes. Visitors are not permitted to enter the sanctuary on their own, but with a docent they can ascend the stairs into the sanctuary area.

sites.name: Holy Trinity Orthodox Cathedral
sites.note:
The church will be open for self-guided tours, with parishioners available to answer questions. Regular scheduled tours are available on Eventbrite for signup by Trained Docents.
https://www.eventbrite.com/e/holy-trinity-orthodox-cathedral-tour-tickets-1109170120689?aff=oddtdtcreator

ENTRANCE RESTRICTIONS: No hats, food, drinks, or pets allowed

sites.name: House of Blues
sites.note: Guests may take a self-guided tour throughout four floors of the venue including the exclusive Foundation Room VIP Club, Music Hall and House of Blues Restaurant & Bar. Live Music starts at 12pm in the restaurant.

sites.name: Hyde Park Art Center
sites.note: Exhibitions will be open and on view. People are welcome to take a self-guided tour, stop at the cafe, and explore the collection of art books in the library.

sites.name: Hyde Park Bank & Trust
sites.note: Visitors are invited to explore the second-floor bank lobby.

sites.name: Hyde Park Union Church
sites.note: Visitors will have access to the sanctuary to view the architecture and stained-glass windows. A continuous video will play, featuring the church's music director in the organ room.

sites.name: Héctor Duarte Studio
sites.note: Visit Duarte's working studio to view completed and in-process artworks and the outdoor mural. Walk yourself through or take a guided tour with the artist.

sites.name: Ignite Glass Studios
sites.note: Event studio, garden, rooftop and gallery spaces will be open for guided or self-guided tours. Guests should enter through the garden gate. Live glassblowing demos will take place during OHC hours, with a narrator sharing information and answering questions. There will also be hands-on glassblowing slots available for purchase either ahead of time or day-of in-person.

sites.name: Illinois Tech's S.R. Crown Hall
sites.note: The main level of Crown Hall is open to guests walking through. Students may be working in the studios at that time and should not be photographed or disturbed. The lower level (where restrooms are located) is open for use of these facilities.

sites.name: Ingersoll-Blackwelder House
sites.note:
Volunteer Docents can answer questions about the history of the house and community and provide information on this important Chicago resource.

A 2025 contest helped choose a color palette for the eventual exterior restoration of the home. The winning submissions will be on display.

sites.name: International Museum of Surgical Science
sites.address: 1524 N. Lake Shore Dr., Chicago, IL 60610
sites.note: The entire museum will be open for self-guided tours.

sites.name: Intuit Art Museum
sites.note: The lower-level, first-floor and second-floor galleries will be open. Guests can also engage with hands-on activities designed in connection with the exhibitions on view in the Center for Learning and Engagement (CLEO).

sites.name: Irish American Heritage Center
sites.note:
Visitors will enjoy a largely self-guided, station-by-station experience throughout the Irish American Heritage Center, enhanced by staff and volunteers providing historical and cultural information.

There will also be demonstrations and cultural activities throughout the day.

The elevator is currently out of service. Upper levels of this building will only be accessible via stairs. Please plan accordingly.

sites.name: Jane Addams Hull-House Museum
sites.note: The Jane Addams Hull-House will be open all weekend for exploration and special activations. Hull-House staff will be on-site to answer questions and offer short tours about the building’s history and construction. Paying homage to bookbinder and Hull-House co-founder, Ellen Gates Starr, Regin Igloria will offer a drop-in community book binding workshop in the Residents’ Dining Hall on Saturday. Sunday will feature seed-cleaning and art making with one of the exhibition's featured Artist Olly Costello. Also on display will be artwork from our workshop series with the artists from Red Line Service, and temporary exhibitions "Perennial City: Experiments in Urban Gardening" and "Act Well Your Part, There All The Honor Lies.

sites.name: Japanese American Service Committee
sites.note:
Visitors are welcome to take a self-guided tour. JASC Staff and volunteer docents will be stationed throughout to share more about the building and JASC programs.

View multiple flower arrangements throughout the building created by students of Ms. Yuko Inoue Darcy of The Ohara School of Ikebana. Chicago Chapter Founder Unshin Ophara (1861-1916) aimed to develop a style of Ikebana that expresses the beauty of natural scenery.

sites.name: Joan W. and Irving B. Harris Theater
sites.note: Enjoy a self-guided tour of the lobby spaces, Guthman Gallery Hallway, and auditorium for a closer look at the architecture and visual art in the spaces. Discounts on tickets to future performances will be sold on-site.

sites.name: John H. Vanderpoel Art Association
sites.note: Explore the museum’s rare collection of over 600 pieces of American art by prominent artists like Grant Wood, Mary Cassatt, Maxfield Parrish, Daniel Chester French, and Lorado Taft, alongside Vanderpoel. Also on view will be “Incantations”, an exhibit featuring a trio of Chicago artists, Lisa Barcy, Nellie Seigel, and Paloma Trecka. Their works explore themes of devotion, memory, and humor through abstract and visually rhythmic collage. Guided tours will be available.

sites.name: Judson & Moore Distillery
sites.address: 3057 N. Rockwell Ave., BLDG 5, Chicago, IL 60618
sites.note: View the distillery operations, including mill room, still room, and barrel room, and purchase cocktails in the tasting room and bottle shop. Staff will be stationed in each room to answer questions.

sites.name: KAM Isaiah Israel
sites.note:
The newly restored and landmarked Sanctuary will be open. Photography is permitted. 

The building will offer timed entry, and visitors will walk through a metal detector. Please do not bring bags, and there is no coat check available.

sites.name: Kehrein Center for the Arts
sites.note: Visitors can tour the auditorium and view any art installations that are present at the time.

sites.name: Kenar Studio
sites.note: OHC visitors are invited to take a self-guided tour of the two levels of galleries featuring current and past retrospective and interactive art of Jerzy Kenar.

sites.name: KOVAL Distillery
sites.note:
OHC 2026 Limited Edition Maple Syrup Cask finished Rye Whiskey will be available for purchase, with a portion of the proceeds going to support the CAC. 
The distillery floor will be open to guests, with team members available to answer questions, offer tastings, and help navigate the self-guided tour. 
Staff will assist with guest flow and verify IDs for all spirit tastings.

sites.name: Lake Effect Brewing Company
sites.note: The brewing area is visible but will not be open. Pints, flights, and to-go beer will be for sale, and water will be offered.

sites.name: Lake View Presbyterian Church
sites.note: The sanctuary will be open and volunteer docents will give optional tours.

sites.name: Legacy Charter School
sites.note: Meet Legacy Scholar Ambassador docents who will lead tours and share what makes their school so special.

sites.name: Lillstreet Art Center
sites.note:
Lillstreet will be open on all three floors, including three gallery spaces, retail shop, art-lined hallways, and select classrooms. Visitors are welcome to take a self-guided tour using maps provided by the front desk. 

Classes will be in session during the event, and signage will indicate rooms not to be entered during the weekend.

sites.name: Ling Shen Ching Tze Buddhist Temple
sites.note: Visitors will be encouraged to enjoy a primarily self-guided experience throughout the temple. Most public rooms and shrine chambers dedicated to different Buddhas and Buddhist deities will be open for viewing. Limited staff and volunteers will be available to answer questions and provide information.

sites.name: LJC Design & Engineering
sites.note: The 15th-floor studio will be open for visitors to explore at their own pace, with LJC architects available throughout the space to answer questions and provide context. Small, guided tours of the 26th floor will be offered from 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM, featuring expansive city and river views.

sites.name: Luther Memorial Church
sites.note: Guests are welcome to explore the sanctuary on their own. There will be placards with details about various items of interest and church members to answer questions or provide assistance.

sites.name: Mana Contemporary Chicago
sites.note: Multiple exhibitions will be on display throughout the building along with many open studios.

sites.name: McCormick Bridgehouse & Chicago River Museum
sites.note: All five floors of the museum, plus its gear room, will be open to the public. Tours are self-guided with docents available for questions.

sites.name: McCormick Place Rooftop Farm
sites.note: The rooftop farm is located on the 5th floor of the McCormick Place West Building. Guests will move through the space at their own pace and staff will be available to answer questions.

sites.name: Mobile Makers Chicago
sites.note: Visitors may take a self-guided tour and enjoy a design/architecture related drop-in activity.

sites.name: Monadnock Building
sites.note:
The Monadnock Building teams up with Chicago Fashion Week for a fashion-focused walk through history. Guests can explore the building's grand first-floor Lobby, stopping in at participating shops and studios for discoveries, a closer look at their work and a glimpse behind the scenes. 

At Optimo's flagship store and showroom, learn about the exacting process of measuring and fitting a custom hat. Field & Florist invites visitors into an interactive exploration of its small-batch and international niche fragrance collection. 

At The Shoe Hospital, see how fine footwear is restored and kept in service for years. At Florodora, discover a curated collection of women's clothing, shoes and accessories from independent designers. 

At Zeglio, explore the inner construction of a bespoke garment, from its linings and hidden layers to the hand stitching behind a precise fit. 

At Monadnock ArtWorks from 11-3, meet artist Patrice Olsen and explore her paintings, drawings and techniques.

sites.name: Muddy Waters MOJO Museum
sites.address: 4339 S. Lake Park Ave., Chicago, IL 60653
sites.note: Some exhibits on the museum's ground floor and a portion of the basement area will be open for self-guided exploration. Musical performances and other programming is anticipated outside in the MOJO Healing Garden.

sites.name: Narrow Bridge Arts Club
sites.note: Narrow Bridge Arts Club will be open for self-guided tours. Visitors are invited to explore, learn, and create alongside artists, activating the building and engage with a new exhibition by Architecture for Public Benefit. To celebrate the skills, creativity, and generosity of Narrow Bridge Art Club, members will lead activities.

sites.name: National Hellenic Museum
sites.note:
Visit the new exhibition, The Odyssey Reimagined, which features the work of eighteen contemporary artists, working across painting, sculpture, photography, textiles, and sound, each responding to Homer’s nearly 3,000-year-old, Odyssey. 

Guests are invited to explore the entire museum including the rooftop (weather permitting). Guided tours will also be available at the top of every hour. 

Additionally, the museum will offer a special experience in the classroom studio where children and adults can participate in hands-on activities that connect ancient Greek culture to the present time. Activities include: 

Into the Modern: Using architectural forms found in Ancient Greek structures, as well as modern forms, visitors can create their own unique city skyline. 

Paint Like an Ancient Potter: Learn about traditional Greek motifs in Ancient Greek pottery, such as meanders, waves, and the symbolism of wheat and olive branches and try your own hand at classical design using paint pens to decorate small clay pots.

sites.name: National Public Housing Museum
sites.note:
Visitors can enjoy a self-guided visit of all of the museum’s exhibits and installations. Museum highlights include architectural artifacts salvaged from the Jane Addams Homes, oral history listening stations where former residents share memories of Edgar Miller’s Animal Court sculptures, and a chance to browse and play our collection of records from musicians who grew up in public housing. 

Visitors can also get a peek at three recreated apartments. These historic apartments share the stories of different families who lived in the Jane Addams Homes between 1938 and 1975. Normally accessible only as part of an interactive guided tour, the apartments will be open for free, self-guided exploration.

sites.name: New Mount Pilgrim Missionary Baptist Church
sites.note: Guests will be able to view the Sanctuary, with hosts available to answer questions and guide guests.

sites.name: Nichols Tower at Homan Square
sites.note: The 14th floor and common areas on all floors will be open for self-guided tours, and art will be displayed on the 3rd floor.

sites.name: Nicky's of Beverly
sites.note: Visitors are welcome to walk throughout the restaurant at their leisure and may order elevated street fare, gelato, and a variety of craft beer, cocktails on tap to enjoy in the dining areas and the patio.

sites.name: Oak Woods Cemetery
sites.note: The cemetery grounds and the mausoleum will be open to visitors. The office will also be open each day until 3 PM on Saturday and 2 PM on Sunday.

sites.name: Olson Kundig
sites.address: 954 W. Washington Blvd., Suite 700, Chicago, IL 60607
sites.note:
Visitors are invited to explore the studio and view project exhibits, physical models, and drawings. The firm's short film "Counterweight" will be on view.

Olson Kundig staff will be available throughout the weekend to discuss the firm's work.

sites.name: One North Dearborn
sites.note: Visitors will have self-guided access to the rooftop lounge and deck, offering skyline views of the city. Enjoy viewing the rooftop veggie garden, learning about the organic beehives, and playing lawn games.

sites.name: OPEN Center for the Arts
sites.note: Visitors may enjoy self-guided tours of OPEN's seasonal and permanent exhibitions, stage, patio, and studio. A community-based artist will also lead guests in a hands-on activity.

sites.name: Orchestra Hall at Chicago Symphony Center
sites.note: Visitors will have access to the Michigan Avenue lobby and Adams Street passage, Orchestra Hall, Richard and Helen Thomas Club, Grainger Ballroom, Ling Z. and Michael C. Markovitz  Arcade, Buntrock Hall, Rotunda and the Forte event space. There will be self-guided and station by-station information. Learn and play in the kids’ space in Buntrock Hall (recommended for ages 3-12.), featuring special activities, videos, coloring stations and scavenger hunt worksheets. Enjoy live music presented by the Chicago Symphony Negaunee Music Institute and behind-the-scenes fireside chats in Grainger Ballroom. Participate in a blood drive featuring Abbott’s mixed reality experience with original music performed by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra.

sites.name: Our Lady of Sorrows Basilica & National Shrine
sites.note: Visits can enjoy a self-guided tour. Greeters will be available to answer questions.

sites.name: Palmisano Park
sites.note: A welcome table will be at the park entrance by 27th and Halsted. Visitors can walk and explore on their own, or participate in short guided tours offered by the conservation nonprofit, Openlands, and landscape architect firm, Site Design Group. Openlands will lead informal nature walks throughout the day, highlighting native plants and wildlife while Site Design will be giving short walking tours discussing the design, engineering, and history of the park. Tours will leave from the welcome table at 11:00 am, 1:00 pm, and 3:00 pm.

sites.name: Park Castles Condominiums
sites.note: Visitors are invited to see the extravagant indoor pool and wander the front courtyards.

sites.name: Perkins&Will
sites.address: 410 N. Michigan Ave., Suite 1600, Chicago, IL 60611
sites.note: Brief staff-led guided tours will be offered of the firm's studio space, model shop, and social spaces on floors 16, 17, and 18.

sites.name: Pru
sites.note: Visitors will have access to the indoor amenity lounge and rooftop terrace located on the 11th floor of One Pru, weather permitting.

sites.name: Pui Tak Center

sites.name: Pullman National Historical Park
sites.note:
Temporary exhibits on display: 

House Histories of Pullman: Step back in time and get to know past residents by tracing the history of original Pullman-built homes. 

A Grave of Stone and Iron: Digging up what we know, and what we don't, about what lies beneath the surface of George Pullman's grave at Graceland Cemetery.

sites.name: Pullman State Historic Site, Illinois State Museum and Historic Sites
sites.note:
Pullman State Historic Site staff will offer visitors a rare glimpse inside the remaining walls of the Rear Erecting Shops. Guides will connect the past and present by providing historical context, explaining current restoration efforts, and facilitating interactive activities for visitors to learn more about the work of historic industrial archeology. Visitors must wear hard-soled, closed-toe footwear; hard hats will be provided.

New in 2026: Historic Industrial Archaeology at the Pullman Car Works.  Current and recent historic industrial archaeology work will be featured, including activities for families.   

Curator-led tours will begin at the east entry plaza of the Pullman State Historic Site parking lot. The co-located Pullman National Historical Park visitor center will also be open for visitors.

Please note this site does not allow priority access.

sites.name: Quinn Chapel
sites.note:
The main fellowship hall on the first floor will be accessible as well as the historic auditorium on the second floor. Quinn Chapel will offer a self-guided, station by station experience for 50 visitors at a time.

On Saturday, October 17, only, the GraceNote Collective gospel choir will provide 15 minute musical presentations at 1:30pm, 2:00pm, 2:30pm, and 3:00pm.

sites.name: Revolution Workshop
sites.note: Revolution Workshop's entire space will be open to visitors, with staff on hand to answer questions.

sites.name: Ridge Historical Society
sites.note:
Visitors can view the grounds from the Seeley Avenue entrance and down to Longwood Drive, step out onto the terraces, and imagine what life was like along Longwood Drive, home to many mansions built above the Blue Island Ridge.

Three first floor spaces will be open to view: the entry hall, dining room, and living room, which is the main gallery space featuring the "50th Anniversary of the Ridge Historic District” exhibit. Visitors can pickup a guide to historic buildings in the Beverly - Morgan Park for a self guided tour, and short exterior tours will be offered every half hour.

sites.name: Right Bee Cider
sites.note: Guests can explore the cidery at their own pace, with occasional tours offered to larger groups.

sites.name: Saint Ignatius College Prep
sites.note: Visitors are invited to tour the ground floor of the main 1869 building, and the fourth-floor Grand Gallery, Brunswick Room and the Foglia Library.

sites.name: Sears Sunken Garden

Visitors may also pick up a map at the Sunken Garden (weather permitting) or at the Tower and complete a self-guided tour of the three sites.

sites.name: Second Presbyterian Church
sites.note: The sanctuary will be open for both self-guided and "station" tours, where visitors will hear more about the site from trained docents at different points in the sanctuary.

sites.name: Segundo Ruiz Belvis Cultural Center
sites.note: The main venue space, which once operated as a theater, will be open to visitors. Enjoy periodic musical performance.

sites.name: Seventeenth Church of Christ, Scientist
sites.note: Visitors may explore the lobby and main sanctuary space.

sites.name: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)
sites.address: 224 S. Michigan Ave., Suite 1000, Chicago, IL 60604
sites.note: SOM Chicago will open its doors on Saturday to guided tours. Tours will feature the 10th floor studios as well as the Interiors and Materials library on the 9th floor.

sites.name: Smart Museum of Art, The University of Chicago
sites.note: Lobby galleries and main galleries will be open. Tours are self-guided through Bloomberg Connects and print guides.

sites.name: Smashed Plastic Record Pressing
sites.note: The pressing room, listening room, and packaging room will be open and available to tour. One or two presses will be running so that participants can get a full demonstration of how records are produced, quality-controlled, and assembled. Owners will be on-site to answer questions about the facility and the building history.

sites.name: South Side Sanctuary
sites.address: 4702 S. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr. , Chicago, IL 60615
sites.note:
South Side Sanctuary is a 13,000 square foot outdoor community campus that demonstrates how vacant urban land can be transformed into vibrant civic infrastructure. For decades, neighbors carved walking paths through the empty lot. Today, those same paths are reimagined and lined with art walls, open-air classrooms, native gardens, performance space, and sensory landscaping that honors the quiet history of movement through space.

The site features a public stage, pollinator-filled living fences, free community Wi-Fi, and flexible outdoor seating. Weekly programs include farmers markets, youth showcases, wellness classes, and live art activations.

The site was designed and developed by Cecilia Cuff and The Nascent Group in partnership with Future Firm Architects as a living laboratory for equitable development, public health, entrepreneurship, arts and culture, and community gathering. Since opening, the space has welcomed over 25,000 visitors and supported over 500 minority owned small businesses.

sites.name: St. Andrew Greek Orthodox Church
sites.note: The main church and chapel will be open to visitors. Self guided tours and informational signage will be placed throughout the space.

sites.name: St. Benedict the African Roman Catholic Church
sites.note: The main church will be open for touring.

sites.name: St. Helen Roman Catholic Church
sites.note: The main floor of the church will be open to visitors for self-guided tours with stations describing the architectural elements of the church.

sites.name: St. James Episcopal Cathedral
sites.note: The Cathedral and St. Andrew's Chapel (entrance on Huron) will both be open.

sites.note: Visitors are invited to explore the church's vestibule and nave, with available handouts discussing the building's history as well as the representations of the paintings, sculptures and stained glass windows. Volunteers will be present to answer questions and provide guided tours upon request.

sites.name: St. Mary of Perpetual Help Roman Catholic Church

sites.name: St. Mary of the Lake Roman Catholic Church
sites.note:
There will be options for both self-guided and guided tours of the apse, nave, and chapel.

The main church and side chapel will be open. A QR code will link to additional information about the site. Tours are largely self-guided but volunteers will be on hand to answer questions.

sites.name: St. Michael in Old Town Roman Catholic Church

sites.name: St. Pauls United Church of Christ
sites.note: View the Sanctuary/Narthex space, the gymnasium, Wieboldt Hall, the Chapel, and reception room. There will be displays, brochures, and self-guided tour information, with the possibility of guided tours.

sites.name: St. Thomas the Apostle Roman Catholic Church

Volunteers stationed throughout the office will be available to answer questions, share insights about Stantec's projects and practice areas, and provide background on the history of both the studio and the Railway Exchange Building.

sites.name: Starling by Duo/.
sites.note: Guests will have access to explore the building on a self-guided tour.

sites.name: Starshaped Press

sites.note: See a working letterpress studio and the materials that make this happen, ranging from the small tools and extensive wood and metal type collection, to prints and books. A Chicago-made press will be in operation and so guests can take a souvenir print. Existing prints and stationery are also available for purchase.

sites.name: Stony Island Arts Bank

sites.name: Sulzen Fine Art Studio

sites.note:
Visitors will have limited access to the former factory converted to live-work studio space for local artists. Chat with artists about the space and their work.

Get an introduction to the history and architectural remnants of this small neighborhood factory and view historic interior photographs from when the space was used as an airbrush factory.

sites.name: Temple Sholom
sites.address: 3480 N. Lake Shore Dr., Chicago, IL 60657
sites.note: Guests may view around the stained glass, roam the hallways, and visit the grand sanctuary.

sites.name: The Arts Club of Chicago

sites.name: The Auditorium

sites.note: Guests will be able to explore The Auditorium Front of House over all 6 floors. No on-stage or back-stage access. An informational print-out will aid self-guided exploration, highlighting key areas and facts.

sites.name: The CheckOut
sites.note: ACM has transformed our popular Sunday afternoon Solo Piano Spotlight concerts into a weekend-long extravaganza for Open House Chicago.  Every fifteen or twenty minutes pianists will perform a wide range of short pieces on our 9 foot concert grand Yamaha piano.   We'll also be on hand to talk about the transformation of the space from a long-empty eyesore to a thriving musical venue including insights into the acoustical treatment.

sites.name: The Chicago Board of Trade Building
sites.note: The first-floor lobby and museum and the vault on the lower level will be open to visitors for self-guided tours.

sites.name: The Cliff Dwellers Club
sites.address: 200 S. Michigan Ave., Suite #2200, Chicago, IL 60604
sites.note: Guests may take a self-guided tour of the 22nd floor club space and terrace, with art and historical artifacts on display. Club members will be on hand to answer questions and speak about the history.

sites.name: The Driehaus Museum's Murphy Auditorium
sites.note: Guests will enter through the Murphy Auditorium's street level entrance at 50 E Erie. Please note there are a few stairs once inside the building. An alternative accessible entrance is just west of the main entrance.

sites.name: The Forum
sites.note:
Tour the iconic Forum Hall, which embodies 125+ years of South Side history, as it moves towards rehabilitation while enjoying a full program of live musical performances. 

Quarter-scale reproductions of the recently discovered opening day scenic backdrops will be on view. Visitors may also tour sections of the West Annex, which reopened in 2026, and engage with community stories playing on the new "Train of Thoughts" digital screen.

sites.name: The House of Glunz & The Glunz Tavern
sites.note: Family members will explain the historic artifacts which adorn the walls and ceilings of both The House of Glunz and The Glunz Tavern.

sites.name: The Moody Church
sites.note: The main lobby and the Sanctuary will be open for guided tours. If desired, visitors can see the adjacent Memorial Hall.

sites.name: The Palette & Chisel Academy of Fine Arts
sites.note: Painting & Sculpting Demos: Between 10am and 5pm on both days, several teachers and members will be painting and sculpting from live models in the second-floor studio, third floor studio, and coach house studio.

sites.name: The Pittsfield Building
sites.note: Visit the building's atrium and second floor, enhanced by volunteers guiding people along and offering explanation.

sites.name: The Plant

sites.name: The Weaving Mill

sites.name: Third Unitarian Church

sites.name: TimeLine Theatre

The rehearsal room and theatre may be limited or off access due to production activities during certain times. Optional guided tours, lasting 30-45 minutes will be offered at set times.

sites.name: Trinity United Methodist Church
sites.note: Visitors are welcome to tour the education wing, great hall, kitchen, parlor, main sanctuary, chapel, organ loft, and courtyard. A brochure will summarize the more than 150 year history of the Trinity Congregation.

sites.name: UChicago Rockefeller Memorial Chapel

sites.name: Ukrainian Institute of Modern Art

sites.name: Ukrainian National Museum

sites.name: United Church of Hyde Park

sites.name: Uptown Theatre
sites.note:

sites.name: Westtown Center
sites.note: Visitors are welcome to explore the program space, meet members, and make artwork with them. The art on display will also be available for sale.

sites.name: Wild Blossom Meadery & Winery
sites.note: Visit the Meadery to learn about the production and beekeeping, and to enjoy tastings.

sites.name: Wild Mile

Urban Rivers volunteers will give tours every 60 minutes, covering the site's history, design, environmental impact, and much more. Families can also enjoy a table activity at the start of the boardwalk.

sites.name: Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven Foundation (Chess Records)

sites.name: Woman's Athletic Club of Chicago

sites.name: Zen Buddhist Temple

sites.name: Zhou B Art Center

The 2nd floor will open after 1pm, with an exhibit on Hispanic Heritage on display. The lower level, 3rd, and 4th floors have artist studios which guests are free to visit if the artist has their studio open.
